title: Slide down the line

predict.q: Illustrative data: P = 10 − Q. As the point moves down the line from P = 8 to P = 2, what happens to PED?

options.s: It stays the same: the slope is constant
options.fb: The slope is constant, but PED also depends on P ÷ Q, which falls as you move down the line.
PED falls in size from −4 at P = 8, to −1 at P = 5, to −0.25 at P = 2, while the slope stays −1.
Moving down, a 1-unit price cut is a bigger % of a lower price, and the extra unit is a smaller % of a bigger quantity. So PED shrinks in size: from 4 to 0.25.

options.s: It changes, but it jumps from elastic to perfectly inelastic at the midpoint
options.fb: PED changes smoothly. It is −1 at the midpoint and reaches 0 only where the line meets the quantity axis.

task: Drag the **price** slider down the line and watch the PED readout and the elastic / unitary / inelastic label.

target.do: Move the price slider down to 2, then press Check.

takeaway: On a straight-line demand curve PED falls in size as price falls: elastic, then unitary at the midpoint, then inelastic.
